text:
incident-bot: P1 page: high tail latency + 503s observed from prod-inference in us-west-2. Alert group: kv-cache & batch-scheduler. Thresholds crossed: 99.9th latency > 4s, error-rate spike to 2% over baseline. Auto-escalation to oncall. link: https://grafana/redwood/d/kvcache/kv-cache-overview

Keira: I'm the on-call for infra this cycle, taking it. Seeing the same in the dashboard. Short requests (<=64 tokens) are queueing behind long streaming requests. KV cache size also trending up ~3x in last 30m.

Sanjay: @Keira grabbing traces. Initial hunch: continuous-batching window got widened in last deploy and prefetch increased hot-set pressure, combined with mixed-request fairness regressions in the scheduler.

Miguel: Customer impact: several Dedicated customers reported higher text-gen tail latency and a handful of 503s. No broad outage but SLA risk. We're getting support tickets.

Keira: Immediate mitigations proposal (short list):
- disable KV prefetch for affected model-routings
- narrow continuous_batching.window_ms -> 25ms from 200ms (reduces head-of-line blocking)
- enable per-queue fairness alpha temporarily (scheduler flag)
- rolling restart batch-scheduler in us-west-2 after config push

Sanjay: Agreed. I'll patch console-config for the model group and flip prefetch. Pushing a hotfix branch.

Sanjay: Pushing config:```bash
# toggle prefetch off for model group: conversational-prod
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_API' -d '{"model_group":"conversational-prod","kv_prefetch":false}' 
  https://admin.redwood/api/v1/runtime/configs
```
Response: 200 OK.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: config-update/conv-prefetch-off at commit 7ac4f2. Rolling to us-west-2 (3 clusters).

ops-bot: Change acknowledged. Will auto-apply scheduler flag 1 minute after config rollout to avoid thrash.

Keira: While that rolls, we should shrink continuous_batching window. Sanjay can you set window_ms=25 and max_batch_tokens=4096? That should reduce HTOL for short requests.

Sanjay: On it. Patching runtime flags. Command:```bash
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/inference-runtime CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=25 CONT_BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=4096 --record
```
Rolling restart scheduled.

Miguel: Support note draft for affected customers (quick):
"We're investigating a spike in tail latency affecting generation for some requests in us-west-2. We've applied a configuration change to reduce batching window and disabled aggressive prefetch to reduce cache pressure. We'll follow up with a full RCA."

Anna: I'll send that to customer success + open a status page incident note. Keeping wording conservative.

Keira: Observability: If latency doesn't start falling in ~3 mins after config/rollout, escalate to rollback to previous scheduler binary. Watch these metrics: kv_cache_size, continuous_batch_queue_depth, batch_wait_ms_p50/p99, request_503_count.

~4m later

Sanjay: Deploy of config and env changes completed across clusters. deploy-bot shows rolling restarts succeeded.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: config-update/conv-prefetch-off. All pods ready.

Sanjay: Quick grep of logs after restart showing fewer long-lived batch locks. Sample log:```
[2026-06-18T12:17:21Z] INFO batch-scheduler: dequeued batch size=7 total_tokens=123 latency_ms=18
[2026-06-18T12:17:21Z] INFO kv-cache: prefetch skipped for model=conversational-prod key_prefix=xyz
```

Keira: Grafana: tail latency dropping. 99.9th went from ~4.2s -> ~900ms within two minutes. KV cache growth plateaued. Error-rate trending down.

Miguel: I'm seeing customer ticket follow-ups — initial replies sent. No new severity escalations.

Anna: Status page update posted: "Mitigation applied; service performance improving. Engineers continuing investigation."

Keira: Root cause notes (short term): a config change in last release widened continuous batching window (intended to improve throughput for large-batch workloads) but interacted poorly with an increase in KV prefetch aggressiveness. For mixed long/short workloads the scheduler's fairness heuristics allowed long requests to hold batches longer than before, starving short requests and causing tail spikes. KV prefetch exacerbated memory pressure and caused transient KV eviction storms.

Sanjay: Follow-ups we need:
- revert the cont-batch window change in the next release unless we can implement size-aware windowing
- add a hard cap on prefetch concurrency per model group
- add an automatic per-request priority bump if request latency > X ms in queue (mitigates starvation)
- create a synthetic test that mixes long + short workload to catch this in perf CI

Keira: I'll file a postmortem ticket and assign owners. Sanjay owns scheduler fairness patch, Miguel owns customer comms, Anna owns status page and ticket triage.

Sanjay: Quick patch note: adding a short-term scheduler flag `fairness_preempt_threshold_ms=150` and enabling it in prod as we test the larger change. Rolling that in now.

ops-bot: Flag set in us-west-2 groups. Flag change will persist until explicitly turned off.

Keira: Confirming end-state:
- KV prefetch disabled for conversational-prod 
- continuous_batch_window narrowed to 25ms 
- scheduler fairness preempt flag enabled 
- rolling restarts completed
- tail latency and error rates returned to baseline

Miguel: Re customer impact: One Dedicated customer had ~12 requests fail with 503s, support credited 24 hours per SLA for their incident line item. Other customers saw elevated latency but no retries needed.

Anna: I'll coordinate the support credits and follow-up messaging.

Keira: Thanks everyone. We'll continue with the RCA doc; expected follow-up: postmortem summary + proposed fixes + timeline in the next 48h. Marking thread as in mitigation/monitoring. If any regressions, ping this thread. :raised_hands:

Sanjay: Logging the incident in incidents repo with runbook pointers.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigation applied. Auto-close timer set for 6 hours unless a new alert reopens.

Keira: Ending oncall handoff note: I'll remain watching for another 30m then hand back to normal rotation. Thanks all.
